sections.overview: The Black-throated Thrush breeds across eastern Eurasia and migrates south to Central and South Asia for winter.
sections.identification: The male has a grey back, white belly and black throat and chest; the female is brown-streaked below and lacks the male’s black throat.
sections.habitat: It breeds in damp coniferous and mixed forests, often with dense undergrowth; in winter it also uses scrub, river woods and parks.
sections.diet: It takes invertebrates in the warm season and relies heavily on berries and other fruits in winter.
sections.behavior: Outside the breeding season it often gathers in flocks, sometimes alongside other thrushes.
sections.reproduction: The regional accounts consulted focus on migration and wintering and give little detail about nesting.
sections.ecology: Central Asian winter flocks can include Fieldfares (T. pilaris); see that profile for this shared winter setting.
sections.conservation: The BTO lists it as Least Concern globally, while noting that it is a very rare vagrant in Britain.
